title: Voice Training
titleZh: 戏剧专业学生的语音训练

parts.label: Part 3
parts.article:
Part three. You will hear a discussion between Fiona, who is the head of a college drama department, and a new tutor called Ed, who is preparing to run a voice coaching workshop for drama students.

First, you have some time to look at questions twenty-one to twenty-six.

Now listen carefully and answer questions twenty-one to twenty-six.

Right. Ed, well, I'm delighted that you've joined the drama department. Now, part of my job is to support you during your probationary year. So let's ensure that you're clear about what you'll be doing in the first voice coaching workshop you run next week.

Okay.

I'll be observing you working with the students as you show them how to project their voices on stage. I'll be evaluating how you cope with the practical activities as well as the theory, and if all goes well, you'll then have finished the final stage of your voice coach diploma.

That'd be great, Fiona. Anyway, I've thought through the workshop, and I've done a plan to highlight the key areas I intend to cover.

Good. Let's look at your plan.

Okay, so let's see. I'm glad you've thought about seating patterns. You say you want to begin with the students sitting in star-shaped patterns. That's fine. There are various seating patterns you can use at this stage. I like trainees sitting cross-legged in a circle. Other people like students in rows. But actually, all these can be represented diagrammatically, which would be clearer than going into lots of detailed explanations like you've done here.

Oh, okay. But it doesn't matter which one I use at the beginning of a workshop?

It's whatever you feel comfortable with.

Fine. So in the initial phase, I explain the objectives of the session.

Okay. Then in the first activity, you say they should quickly rise, walk briskly around the room, weaving in and out to avoid each other.

Yes. I think it's important that they don't get in each other's way and that they learn to move within a confined space, aware of other people, but primarily concentrating on their own thoughts.

Absolutely. But in your plan, you've omitted to mention that in the second activity, you will get the students to pair off. So you need to rethink that section and include reasons why it's essential for them to listen to each other talking. It doesn't matter what they actually say, and at the same time, get them to think about their posture because that governs their lung capacity and most crucially, their breathing.

Right. Will do.

Okay. Of course, a common issue in the UK is that we rehearse in small rooms, then transfer to a larger stage. So bearing in mind that voice projection is not shouting, later in the course, you'll need to work in a much bigger space.

Does it have to be an enclosed space? I, I suppose it does because ultimately they're going to work in a theater.

Ideally, an enclosed space, but there's no reason why you couldn't go somewhere outdoors, although I'd avoid a very public space like a park.

Right. Thanks.

Now, your next activity on how to convey emotion on stage is fine, but your selection of texts for the students to experience emotional depth leaves a little to be desired. It's not enough to include a few extracts that you find enjoyable. You need to consider the different kind of emotion that each extract should present, from sorrow through to ecstasy. Classical stuff is all well and good, but include many more contemporary sources.

I understand.

Before you hear the rest of the discussion, you have some time to look at questions twenty-seven to thirty.

Now listen and answer questions twenty-seven to thirty.

Now, out of the twenty books you list, some are more useful than others, and I think you should flag up the disadvantages so that people don't waste money buying them. Take Vocal Instruction. I know I recommended it for you to read for its historical perspective, but bear in mind it was written thirty years ago, and it shows.

Yeah, agreed.

I thought Improve Your Accent was interesting, but it's very narrow in its outlook, don't you think?

Well, I'm not sure it's interesting [chuckles] . And another one you need to warn people about is The Actor's Handbook. It's an expensive book, very useful, but according to the publishers, they're going to reissue it with new color photos, and at the moment, it's out of print. There aren't any second-hand copies out there, so tell them not to waste time looking for it.

Oh, right. I didn't know that.

There's one more that I want to mention, and that's Confident Voice Delivery. It exaggerates its claims on how to be successful to such an extent that I think it is positively misleading. But maybe I'm biased.

[chuckles] Okay, I'll make a note of that. Thanks. So the others...

That is the end of part three. You now have thirty seconds to check your answers to part three.

questions.question: Ed is giving the voice coaching workshop in order to get

analyses.content: 录音中 Fiona 提到，如果一切顺利，Ed 就能完成他的语音教练文凭（diploma）的最后阶段，这里的 diploma 完美对应了选项中的 qualification（资格/学历）。
你可能会因为刚开头听到加入部门（joined the department）而误选 A（新工作），但录音明确说办讲习班是他拿文凭的最后一个环节。

I'll be observing you working with the students as you show them how to project their voices on stage. I'll be evaluating how you cope with the practical activities as well as the theory. And if all goes well, you'll then have finished the final stage of your voice coach diploma.

questions.question: According to Fiona, the seating pattern that Ed chooses

analyses.content: 当 Ed 问是不是一开始用哪种座位安排都无所谓时，Fiona 明确回答“只要你觉得合适就行（whatever you feel comfortable with）”，意思就是选择哪种安排并不特别重要。
你可能会听到 Fiona 说“画图展示会更清晰（represented diagrammatically）”而误选 A，但题目问的是“Ed 选择哪种座位这件事”怎么样，Fiona 最终给这件事的定调是选哪种都行。A 选项说“必须视觉呈现”（should be illustrated visually），这是不对的。
Oh, okay. But it doesn't matter which one I use at the beginning of a workshop. It's whatever you feel comfortable with.

questions.question: Fiona and Ed agree that in the first activity, the students

analyses.content: Ed 提到，最重要的是让学生主要集中于自己的思绪（primarily concentrating on their own thoughts），这直接对应选项中的“把注意力放在自己身上”。
你可能会听到“aware of other people”而觉得是和别人接触（干扰项 B），但句子紧接着用了转折词 but 强调“primarily concentrating on...”，重点仍然是专注自身。

Okay. Then in the first activity, you say they should quickly rise, walk briskly around the room, weaving in and out to avoid each other. Yes. I think it's important that they don't get in each other's way and that they learn to move within a confined space, aware of other people, but primarily concentrating on their own thoughts.

questions.question: Fiona and Ed agree that in the second activity, Ed should

analyses.content: Fiona 建议 Ed 要让学生关注自己的体态，因为这决定了肺活量以及最关键的“呼吸（breathing）”，这直接对应了选项中的 breath control。
你可能会听到“get the students to pair off”或“listen to each other talking”而去看其他选项（比如 A），但这只是活动的形式，Fiona 最终落脚的目的是利用这个形式来训练呼吸。

But in your plan, you've omitted to mention that in the second activity, you will get the students to pair off. So you need to rethink that section and include reasons why it's essential for them to listen to each other talking. It doesn't matter what they actually say. And at the same time, get them to think about their posture because that governs their lung capacity and most crucially, their breathing. Right. Will do.

questions.question: What does Fiona suggest about working in a big space?

analyses.content: Fiona 说理想情况下是封闭空间（室内），但也没理由不能去室外（outdoors），说明室内外都可以。
你可能会因为捕捉到了“park”这个词而激动地去选 B，但 Fiona 的原话是“avoid a very public space like a park”，意思是“要避免去公园”，正好说反了。

Does it have to be an enclosed space? I suppose it does because ultimately they're going to work in a theater. Ideally, an enclosed space, but there's no reason why you couldn't go somewhere outdoors, although I'd avoid a very public space like a park.

questions.question: What does Fiona think of Ed's selection of texts?

analyses.content: Fiona 认为 Ed 选的文本种类不够，需要涵盖从悲伤到狂喜的不同情感，而且不仅要有古典作品还要包含现代作品，这意味着涵盖的范围需要更广。
你可能会听到“Classical stuff”而错选 A，但录音说的是“只有古典的还不够，还要加入更多现代的”，所以核心不是偏向某一种，而是强调范围。

Now, your next activity on how to convey emotion on stage is fine, but your selection of texts for the students to experience emotional depth leaves a little to be desired. It's not enough to include a few extracts that you find enjoyable. You need to consider the different kind of emotion that each extract should present, from sorrow through to ecstasy. Classical stuff is all well and good, but include many more contemporary sources.

Textbooks
27. Vocal Instruction
28. Improve Your Accent
29. Actors' Handbook
30. Confident Voice Delivery

analyses.content: Fiona 评价这本书是三十年前写的，“并且能明显看出来（and it shows）”，这说明它的内容已经过时了。
你可能会因为听到“historical perspective”觉得它有历史价值是个优点，但这道匹配题要选的是缺点（disadvantages），后半句的“三十年前写的”才是对其缺点的最终定性。
Take Vocal Instruction. I know I recommended it for you to read for its historical perspective, but bear in mind it was written thirty years ago, and it shows.
Ed 直接评价这本书的视野“非常狭窄（very narrow in its outlook）”，直接等同于选项中的 too limited。
听到前半句的“interesting”时不要急着下定论，紧跟在转折词 but 后面的内容才是这段话要表达的核心缺点。
I thought Improve Your Accent was interesting, but it's very narrow in its outlook, don't you think?
Fiona 提到这本书目前绝版了（out of print），且外面没有二手书（aren't any secondhand copies），所以目前是买不到的（unavailable）。
你一开始听到“expensive”很容易秒选 A，但接着听会发现他们马上要出新版了，现在市面上根本买不到，所以对于学生来说核心缺点已经变成了“买不到”，不能再去浪费时间找。

And another one you need to warn people about is The Actor's Handbook. It's an expensive book, very useful, but according to the publishers, they're going to reissue it with new color photos, and at the moment it's out of print. There aren't any secondhand copies out there, so tell them not to waste time looking for it.
Fiona 认为这本书在宣传如何成功时夸大了说辞（exaggerates its claims），简直起到了误导的作用，对应选项中的“不切实际的（unrealistic）”。
夸大其词（exaggerates）是这道题唯一的同义替换关键，这里没有太多干扰项，核心就是要准确抓取并理解这个词的情感色彩。

There's one more that I want to mention, and that's Confident Voice Delivery. It exaggerates its claims on how to be successful to such an extent that I think it is positively misleading. But maybe I'm biased.
